chunks: And whatever is in it regarding the mention of rights from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl from Ali ibn al-Husayn, Sayyid al-Abidin (peace be upon them), I have narrated it from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa - may Allah be pleased with him - who said: Muhammad ibn Jafar al-Kufi al-Asadi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Isma'il ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Thabit ibn Dinar al-Thumali, from Sayyid al-Abidin Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them).

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنِ الْفَضْلِ: Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, a key narrator in Shia hadith literature
key_terms.الْحُقُوقِ: Al-Huquq (Rights), referring to the specific legal or spiritual rights discussed in the hadith
key_terms.ثَابِتُ بْنُ دِينَارٍ: Thabit ibn Dinar, a companion of the Imams known as al-Thumali
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: Radiya Allahu 'anhu (May Allah be pleased with him), a phrase often used for Shia narrators in this context
key_terms.سَيِّدِ الْعَابِدِينَ: Sayyid al-Abidin (Master of the Worshippers), a title for Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn

ai.seo_question: What is the narrator chain for the hadith of rights from Ali ibn al-Husayn in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous methodology of Shaykh al-Saduq in verifying the authenticity of the 'Huquq' (Rights) tradition by explicitly tracing its specific transmission through Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, a key figure in the Kufan scholarly network. By detailing the chain from al-Thamali to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn, al-Saduq underscores the reliability of this specific report within the broader corpus of Shia jurisprudence, highlighting the importance of individual narrator verification in establishing legal precedents for social and spiritual obligations.
